disagreements.topic: Did the revisions take up the round-1 findings (and is the convergence real)?
disagreements.positions: All four revised toward round-1 findings. Fair values went from $324-370 to $338-356, thesis breaks from $200-215 to $205-212, and P(>=358) from 0.49-0.52 to 0.495-0.502. The round-2 mean ladder is within 0.5 pt of the round-1 supervisor ladder at every strike.
disagreements.resolution: Each agent took up every feedback item (see revision_check). But the narrowing is mostly the agents adopting the same supervisor inputs. Mean source Jaccard doubled from 0.064 to 0.141, and CNBC Fed, Yahoo OpenAI, the Amazon 8-K and the Q2 8-K are now cited by 3+ agents. So the tighter spread is not new independent confirmation and should not be read as more certainty.
disagreements.evidence: source_overlap.json (round1 vs final); agents' revisions lists.

disagreements.topic: Residual fair-value spread ($338 agent_2 vs $356 agent_4)
disagreements.positions: agent_2 uses 40x on CY28 EPS $8.63 with a residual competition haircut. Agents 1, 4 and 5 use 44-45x on NTM EPS $8.0-8.5. Net cash is now $2.0-2.1B in all four.
disagreements.resolution: Not settleable by search: it is a multiple judgment (about 4 turns = about $35/share on the P/E leg). The factual inputs (Q3 guide, cash, warrant terms, the Trainium4 timeline) now agree across agents. I keep fair value at the forecaster mean, about $349, just under spot.
disagreements.evidence: Q2 2026 8-K Ex. 99.1 and 10-Q; agents' method inputs.

disagreements.positions: P(>=89) ranges 0.96 (agent_5) to 0.975 (agents 2, 4); P(>=143) ranges 0.895 to 0.925. agent_4's bear is $170 but its far tail is the thinnest.
disagreements.resolution: I lean to agent_5, the base-rate lane. ALAB fell 68% in Jan-Apr 2025 and about 40% in Jun-Jul 2026, and Credo fell 52% in 2026. A one-year close below $143 (-60%) at about 3% (agents 2, 4) is light for a 99%-vol, 56x-P/E name with 69% top-3 concentration. Recent bear commentary is valuation-only: a Seeking Alpha 'I'd short it but there's no catalyst' piece, and short interest of about 5.8% of float at Aug 31. There is no new fundamental negative, and the Sep 28 -4.3% move was sector-wide. So I fatten only the far tail, not the median.
disagreements.evidence: agent_5 base-rate sources; Seeking Alpha 4913220; MarketBeat short interest; QuiverQuant Sep 28 move note.

disagreements.positions: All four now put the Q3 print (unannounced) after Oct 29, the Oct 28 FOMC (~70% hike odds) inside the window, late-October hyperscaler capex prints and the OpenAI pause. Medians are $354-356.
disagreements.resolution: Confirmed. No Q3 2026 conference-call announcement had appeared as of Sep 30 (the Q2 call was announced about 2 weeks ahead of Aug 4), so the print most likely falls Nov 3-5, outside the window. The ladders agree within about 1.5 pt, and I keep the mean.
disagreements.evidence: ALAB IR news releases page; Q2 call announcement.

revision_check.agent_1: Took up all three items: Oct 28 FOMC and OpenAI pause added to the 1-month view, net cash cut $2.5B->$2.1B (re-verified in the 10-Q: AR +$109M, inventory +$53M), P>=626 trimmed 0.22->0.20. Fair value $360->$352. Stayed in the primary lane.

revision_check.agent_4: Took up all three: stale Polymarket lean dropped, FOMC added, Substack/TIKR target leg removed from fair value. Fair value $370->$356. Still some newsletter/TIKR material inside the 2027 revenue derivation (AWS $2-3B content) - colour only.
revision_check.agent_5: Took up all three: net cash $2.5B->$2.0B, AWS warrant used in bear/bull and the multiple, Polymarket 'AI bubble' demoted to colour. It checked its 5th percentile against the drawdown base rates and fattened it (P>=89 0.965->0.96).

one_month_reasoning: No ALAB print before Oct 29 (Q3 call not yet announced; likely Nov 3-5). The window holds the Oct 28 FOMC (~70% hike priced), late-October hyperscaler capex prints and the OpenAI pause overhang, so I keep the four agents' converged mean: median about $355, monthly sigma about 25%.
confidence_reason: Round 2 settled no new disagreement that matters. The revisions converged on the round-1 findings, and the remaining spread is a multiple judgment that search cannot resolve. My only change is a 0.5-0.6 pt fattening of the far-left tail for the missing skeptic lane, so the mean stays the anchor.
thesis_break_reason: The four agents give $205-212, all at about 32-33x 2027 consensus EPS of $6.39. Below about $208 the market would be pricing the loss of the ~$3B 2027 revenue path: a lost or double-sourced AWS scale-up socket, a Q4 guide at or below the ~$550M Q3 level, or real hyperscaler capex cuts rather than Fed or AI-sentiment swings.
key_drivers: Q3 2026 guide $540-560M (+40% q/q) and EPS $1.16-1.21; the Q3 print and Q4 guide (~Nov 3-5, Q4 consensus about $655M) are the first hard test of the Scorpio X ramp.
Valuation: about 56x 2027 consensus EPS $6.39. The one-year outcome hinges on whether the multiple compresses to about 40x (agent_2) or 44-45x (others) as growth slows toward 30%.
Concentration: top-3 customers are 69% of Q2 revenue. AWS ties are formalised by a warrant vesting on up to $6.5B of cumulative purchases through 2033, which is a ceiling, not a backlog.
Scale-up fabric competition: UALink (native Trainium4 racks, an ALAB opportunity) versus NVLink Fusion hybrid racks and Broadcom scale-up Ethernet.
Macro and sentiment: a Fed hike about 70% priced for Oct 28 and OpenAI's widened training pause, against no hyperscaler capex cuts so far.

fair_value.reason: All agents now use net cash of $2.0-2.1B and the corrected Trainium4 and warrant facts, so no factual correction remains. Revised fair values are $338 / $352 / $356 / $349 and differ only on the multiple (40-45x NTM EPS of $8.0-8.6). I keep their mean, about $349, about 2% below spot.

Your 40x multiple is the main reason your fair value sits $11-18 below the others. It is a judgment, not an error, but you do not show a peer-multiple base rate for 30%-growth semis to justify it.

changes.why: The skeptic lane is still missing and agents 2/4 put only ~3% on a -60% year, which is light against ALAB's own -68% (2025) and -40% (2026) drawdowns and Credo's -52%; I lean to the base-rate lane (agent_5).

summary: The four revised forecasts took up every round-1 finding and converged: fair values $338-356 (mean ~$349, just under the $357.84 spot), thesis breaks $205-212, and a median at about spot. That convergence largely reflects shared supervisor inputs rather than new independent evidence. The remaining gap is a 40x-vs-45x multiple judgment that search cannot settle. I keep the mean ladder except for a slightly fatter far-left tail to cover the missing skeptic lane; confidence is low. The next real information is the Q3 print and Q4 guide around Nov 3-5, just after the one-month window.

sizing.entry: 2 tranches: half now, half after the Q3 2026 report (~Nov 3-5) if the Q4 guide confirms the Scorpio X ramp
sizing.overlap: None; the portfolio is all cash. This would be the first AI-infrastructure/semis position, so any later NVDA/AVGO/MRVL/CRDO-type buys would share its drivers.
sizing.reason: Fair value is about spot, so there is no margin of safety. On top of that: ~99% realized vol, 56x forward EPS, 69% top-3 concentration, and a Fed decision, hyperscaler capex prints and ALAB's own earnings within about five weeks; a 40-60% drawdown is a base-rate event. Liquidity is ample and the listing (Mar 2024) is past lock-ups, but a single name like this should not exceed 5% of a $10k portfolio.
